layout_dets.text: Machin and Guha: The use of potentiostatic techniques in the development of improved stainless steels for chemical plant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The use of potentiostatic techniques in the development of improved stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels for chemical plant*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By R. Machin**) and P. Guha**)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The behaviour patterns of the common conventional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels, both wrought and cast, in corrosive environ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments, have been established over the years, mainly by long

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: term immersion or exposure tests complemented by service

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiences. Consequently, the development of steels of im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proved corrosion resistance has been a slow process mainly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because of the length of time necessary to produce useful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information from such tests. The introduction and develop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment of potentiostatic techniques, however, in recent years

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have enabled the corrosion behaviour of stainless steels to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studied in a systematic way by tests of short duration. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present paper describes the results of such studies in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Authors' laboratory which firstly correlated the known cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion behaviour of cast stainless steels in general production

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with their potentiostatic characteristics and, secondly, used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the potentiostat extensively to guide and monitor all stages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of developmenț of an improved stainless steel designated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FERRALIUM®1) alloy. This steel was shown to possess an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exceptional resistance to general corrosion in many aggres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive environments and especially to attack in crevices or in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: circumstances normally associated with pitting corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is shown in Fig. 2 in which can also be seen the secondary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active peak at around 50mV which is a characteristic of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels which are wholly or partially ferritic.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. Polarisation characteristics of 18Cr10Ni in 1 N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiostatic Test Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiostatic studies were carried out using a Wenking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiostat. The stepping rate during polarisation was main-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained at 10 mV/min. using a stepping motor. The polarisa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion cell set-up and electrode holder were as recommended

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Greene (1). Polarisation was carried out according to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recommendations of the ASTM G. 1 Committee. All test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions were purged with oxygen-free high purity nitrogen.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All potentials reported are with reference to a Standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Calomel Electrode (S.C.E.).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conventional stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (i) General Corrosion Resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1 illustrates the typical polarisation curve in IN sulph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uric acid of a cast 18Cr10Ni austenitic stainless steel in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annealed condition, showing an active current peak at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -300mV and a passive range extending beyond +800mV.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The passivation of this alloy in oxidizing conditions across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this range has been demonstrated by immersion tests, for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, in 65% nitric acid (corresponding to a potential of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 800mV S.C.E.) and in copper sulphate solution (zero mV

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S.C.E.) (2). It is considered by the authors, that the passiva-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of this type of steel is related to its stable austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microstructure. For comparison, the limited range of passiv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity of a ferritic nickel-free 17% chromium steel (wrought)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2. Polarisation characteristics of 17 Cr ferritic steel in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1NH₂SO₄

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cast 17% Chromium steel containing up to 5% Nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will also show a limited range of passivity and it is only when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8—10% Nickel is introduced that a wide passivation range is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed. With the 18Cr10Ni composition, a stable austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is produced, not subject to breakdown to martensite. Al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: though a small amount of stable ferrite may be present, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: does not have any deleterious effect on the cast alloy's gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eral corrosion behaviour.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Molybdenum additions to the cast 18Cr10Ni steel im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prove its corrosion behaviour in sulphuric acid and, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 3, this is reflected in a reduction of the active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current peak. Comparison of Figs. 1 and 3 demonstrates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the passivity of 18Cr1ONi3Mo cast material is also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintained to above +800mV (S.C.E.) which is similar to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18Cr1ONi steel, thereby indicating that, contrary to general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: opinion, the alloy containing 3% Molybdenum is as resistant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to nitric acid as the Molybdenum-free.

layout_dets.text: The ability to correlate known corrosion behaviour with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiostatic characteristics is further emphasised in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a special cast stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel of basic composition 29% Nickel, 20% Chromium, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including controlled amounts of Copper, Molybdenum and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Niobium. This alloy has been shown in service to have an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exceptionally high resistance to corrosion by sulphuric acid,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. a corrosion rate of less than 0.001 inches/year (0.025

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mm) is shown in all concentrations of sulphuric acid at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: room temperature. This can be correlated with the polarisa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion curve in Fig. 4 where the active current peak extends

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over a much narrower potential range than that shown by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 18Cr10Ni3Mo steel (Fig. 3), implying a low rate of cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion in non-oxidizing conditions. The displacement of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current peak to a more noble potential (-150mV S.C.E.)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrates, in particular, the relative immunity of this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cast alloy to deaerated sulphuric acid at approximately zero

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydrogen potential, i.e. -250m V S.C.E. (2).

layout_dets.text: (ii) Intergranular Corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Susceptibility to intergranular corrosion is normally mea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sured by the Strauss test, wherein the test piece is immersed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in boiling Copper Sulphate solution before bending to detect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any intergranular attack. These corrosive conditions can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simulated by potentiostatic techniques in sulphuric acid at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a potential of zero mV (S.C.E.) (2). Thus Fig. 5 which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows a secondary peak at zero mV in cast 18Cr10Ni 0.07C

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel after a sensitizing heat-treatment at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that this material in this condition would not pass the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Strauss test, i.e. it would be susceptible to intergranular cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion as is well known from actual Strauss tests and from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: service experience. It is also known that this susceptibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be removed by either the addition of a stabilizing ele-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment, e.g. Niobium or Titanium or by reducing the carbon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content of the steel to a low level (0.03% in some specifica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions). Fig. 6 shows however that in the presence of 3%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Molybdenum, even with a Carbon content as high as 0.07%,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the current peak at zero mV is absent and that à cast steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the 18Cr10Ni3Mo composition, even after a sensitizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heat-treatment, will not show intergranular corrosion. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foregoing conclusions have all been confirmed in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Authors' laboratory by practical Strauss tests. No further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 5. Polarisation characteristics of 18Cr10Ni in 1 N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 6. Polarisation characteristics of 18Cr10Ni3Mo in 1 N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement is produced in the 18Cr10Ni3Mo cast steel by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduction of the Carbon content to 0.035% (Fig. 7). These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results show that without need for stabilizing element addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, Carbon contents of up to 0.07% should be acceptable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 18Cr10Ni3Mo stainless steel castings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With regard to the use of stabilizing elements, of which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results of Fig. 8 which shows a polarisation curve of an

layout_dets.text: 18Cr10Ni3Mo1Nb steel indicate an increase in the active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current peak compared with a niobium-free casting (Fig. 3).

layout_dets.text: 18Cr10Ni3Mo steels with up to 0.07% Carbon, would appear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (iii) Pitting Resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting resistance of 18Cr10Ni steel in chloride-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing environments is known from practical experience

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be poor. This can also be demonstrated by potentiostatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests conducted in sodium chloride solution. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 9 shows a breakdown potential of -50mV (S.C.E.) for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a cast 18Cr10Ni steel in 3% sodium chloride solution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 9. Polarisation characteristics of 18Cr10Ni in 3% NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction of Molybdenum to the 18Cr10Ni steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modifies this behaviour and improves the pitting resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in chloride-containing environments, the breakdown poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial being raised to 200mV, as shown in Fig. 10. The im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provement is not however sufficient to eliminate pitting in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: service environments containing chloride.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 10. Polarisation characteristics of 18Cr10Ni3Mo in 3% NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (iv) Ferralium alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Increase of Chromium content from 18% to 25% can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown to produce further improvement in general corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance and pitting resistance of a steel containing 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nickel and 3% Molybdenum and, at this level of Chromium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it has also been demonstrated that reduction of Nickel con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tent to 5% produces an excellent combination of these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties. With adjustments of Molybdenum content and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduction of Copper, an optimum composition has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: derived which produces in this proprietary alloy a duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic-ferritic (50 : 50) microstructure with excellent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to general corrosion, pitting and crevice attack,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: together with high strength and good ductility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This has been designated FERRALIUM alloy and is sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject of Patents in the United Kingdom and other countries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 11 shows the remarkably high breakdown potential of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloy in 3% sodium chloride at approx. +800mV, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the wide passive range in acid conditions, up to approx.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: +1000mV, accompanied by a low active current peak,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in comparison with that of 18Cr10Ni3Mo in 1ON

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sulphuric acid in Fig. 12, indicates the high resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in a wide range of oxidizing and non-oxidizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The second part of this paper will describe how the po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentiostat provided details of the influence of compositional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and processing variables during the development of the new

layout_dets.text: alloy, and thereby assisted in finalising both the composi-

layout_dets.text: tion and the optimum production procedures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloy development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The initial obiect of this development was to produce a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cast stainless steel of high strength and hardness with cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion resistance at least equivalent to that of austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels of the 18Cr10Ni3Mo type. The composition ranges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studied were based on 25 % Chromium, 5% Nickel, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controlled amounts of Molybdenum and Copper. This steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a duplex 50 : 50 austenitic ferritic microstructure,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known to provide high strength, which was enhanced by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduction of a precipitation-hardening mechnism. Stage 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the development determined the effects of variation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition and heat-treatment on mechanical properties.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Preliminary corrosion tests were also carried out during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stage 1 and these demonstrated that, in addition to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excellent combination of mechanical properties available,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloy range being studied possessed corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: superior to that of the 18Cr10Ni3Mo austenitic stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel in many environments and that its pitting resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the presence of chloride was better than that of any aus-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tenitic stainless steel. Potentiostatic studies were thereafter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used in Stage II of the development to optimise composi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and heat-treatment in relation to corrosion resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial current/time studies in sodium chloride solution with

layout_dets.text: steels of varying nickel contents from 3.5—8.5% on a base

layout_dets.text: Further studies showed that heat-treatment and micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure had significant effects on resistance to corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and especially pitting. Fig. 17 shows how the low pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance in chloride of an as-cast structure is raised by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution treatment at 1120 °C. A subsequent ageing treat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment at 500 °C. produces the optimum combination of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanical properties but has little effect on the good pit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting resistance obtained after annealing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At this stage it was concluded that an alloy could be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produced which, when suitably heat-treated, would possess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the required combination of:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (a) High strength

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (b) Good ductility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (c) Good corrosion resistance to oxidizing and non-oxidiz-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing chemical environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (d) High pitting resistance in the presence of chloride ions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition to the successful production of complex cast-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ings, hot and cold working characteristics of the alloy were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studied to enable all wrought forms to be made available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: together with welding consumables for the fabrication of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloy. Potentiostatic tests were used at this stage to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monitor the effects of hot working variables on corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The new alloy has been in commercial production for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several years and constant potential tests are currently used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in production quality control of wrought and cast materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to ensure that a consistently high level of corrosion resis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance and pitting resistance is maintained. The results of po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentiostatic and laboratory controlled immersion tests during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its development have been fully confirmed in field tests and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by commercial applications. The high degree of resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in many aggressive conditions has resulted in its ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tensive use in handling, for example, mineral acids, chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions, hydroxides.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Summary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been shown that the behaviour of cast stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels of various types in a variety of corrosive conditions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be closely correlated with the results of potentiostatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests. Conversely, potentiostatic techniques can accurately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predict the corrosive behaviour of unfamiliar combinations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of alloy and chemical environment. Such techniques provide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an approach to the development of corrosion resistant alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is economic of time, labour and material. They have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been used successfully in the development and production

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality control of a new alloy, which has an exceptionally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: good combination of mechanical properties añd resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to general corrosion and to pitting or crevice attack.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In conclusion, several successful applications of this alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in chemical environments are illustrated in Figs. 18—20.
